4b4f82f0-983e-43d5-afcc-62f0faa405a6.name: Tofu Scramble
4b4f82f0-983e-43d5-afcc-62f0faa405a6.ingredients:
1 block (14 oz) firm tofu, drained
1 cup mushrooms, sliced
1/2 cup bell peppers, diced (choose only green which is low FODMAP)
1/4 cup green onions (green parts only), chopped
1/4 cup fresh coriander leaves, chopped
1 teaspoon turmeric
1/2 teaspoon cumin
1/2 teaspoon paprika
1/4 teaspoon black salt
Salt and pepper to taste
Fresh coriander/ chives, chopped (for garnish)
4b4f82f0-983e-43d5-afcc-62f0faa405a6.steps:
Drain the tofu and wrap it in a clean kitchen towel or paper towels. Gently press to remove excess moisture. Crumble the tofu into small pieces using your hands or a fork.
In a non-stick skillet over medium heat, add a splash of water or vegetable broth to prevent sticking. Add the crumbled tofu and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the sliced mushrooms and diced bell peppers to the skillet. Continue cooking for another 5 minutes until the mushrooms have softened.
Sprinkle turmeric, cumin, paprika, black salt, salt, and pepper over the tofu and vegetables. Stir well to evenly distribute the spices.
Add the green onions and fresh parsley to the skillet. Cook for an additional 2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is well combined and heated through.
Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Remove from heat and garnish with fresh coriander/ chives.
Serve the tofu scramble hot and enjoy!

9102320e-43cf-4b72-9d62-af1972fdae7a.name: Moong daal dosa
9102320e-43cf-4b72-9d62-af1972fdae7a.ingredients:
1 cup split moong dal (yellow lentils), soaked overnight
1/4 cup brown rice flour
1/4 cup water (or as needed for batter consistency)
1/4 cup finely chopped coriander leaves
1/4 cup grated carrot
1/4 cup finely chopped bell pepper, green
1/4 cup finely chopped scallions (green parts only)
1/2 teaspoon grated ginger
1/2 teaspoon cumin seeds
1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
Salt to taste
9102320e-43cf-4b72-9d62-af1972fdae7a.steps:
Rinse the soaked moong dal thoroughly and drain the water.
In a blender, add the soaked moong dal, brown rice flour, water, grated ginger, cumin seeds, turmeric powder, and salt. Blend everything together to form a smooth batter. If the batter is too thick, add a little more water to achieve a pourable consistency. Let it rest for 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the vegetable filling by combining the chopped coriander leaves, grated carrot, bell pepper, and scallions in a separate bowl.
Heat a non-stick or cast-iron skillet on medium heat. Pour a ladleful of the moong dal batter onto the center of the skillet and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin dosa.
Sprinkle a portion of the vegetable filling on top of the dosa, pressing it gently into the batter.
Cover the skillet with a lid and cook the dosa on low heat for 2-3 minutes.
Carefully flip the dosa using a spatula and cook for another 2 minutes on the other side.
Transfer the cooked dosa to a serving plate and repeat the process to make more dosas with the remaining batter and filling.
Serve the moong dal dosas hot with low FODMAP chutney like mint cilantro chutney

7b884c9c-d6f1-40b0-b383-ed8bbe3ba2ba.name: Vegetable Daal
7b884c9c-d6f1-40b0-b383-ed8bbe3ba2ba.ingredients:
1 cup red lentils
2 cups water
1 cup diced tomatoes
1 cup chopped spinach
1 cup chopped cruciferous vegetable (e.g., radish, kale, cauliflower or broccoli)
1 small carrot, diced
1 small zucchini, diced
1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
1 teaspoon cumin powder
1 teaspoon coriander powder
1/4 teaspoon paprika
Salt to taste
Freshly ground black pepper to taste
Chopped fresh cilantro, for garnish
7b884c9c-d6f1-40b0-b383-ed8bbe3ba2ba.steps:
Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under running water to remove any dirt or debris.
In a large pot, add the rinsed lentils and water. Bring it to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and let the lentils simmer for about 15 minutes, or until they are soft and mushy.
Add the diced tomatoes, chopped spinach, cruciferous vegetable, carrot, zucchini, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and paprika (if using) to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Cover the pot and simmer for another 15-20 minutes, or until all the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper according to your taste preferences. Stir well.
Remove from heat and garnish with chopped fresh cilantro.
Serve the vegetable daal hot with brown rice.

bfb58165-8a67-41fe-b02f-75ae510f1bc2.name: SoyBean Curry with Brown Rice
bfb58165-8a67-41fe-b02f-75ae510f1bc2.ingredients:
Soy beans (cooked) 1 cup
Cumin seeds 1/2 Tsp
Ginger 1 Tsp
Tomato 2 medium sized, pureed
1 cup cauliflower florets (boiled)
Turmeric powder- 1 Tsp
Chilly powder 1 tsp
Cumin powder- 1/2 Tsp
Garam masala- 1 Tsp
Salt to taste
Freshly ground black pepper powder to taste
1 cup cooked brown rice
bfb58165-8a67-41fe-b02f-75ae510f1bc2.steps:
Soak the soybeans overnight (one cup of soy bean to 2 cups of water).
Take the soy bean in a pot and add enough water to cover. Add salt, cover with a lid and cook on simmering fire until done.
In the mean time blend together ginger- green chilly paste in food processor, set aside.
Puree the fresh tomatoes and set aside.
Strain the soy bean and reserve the left over cooking liquid.
Heat up a pot and add mustard seeds. Let it crackle and add cumin seeds.
Then add turmeric powder, cumin powder, chilly powder and salt. Cook for 5 minutes and add tomato puree and cauliflower. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Now it's time to add the cooked soy beans and left over cooking liquid (broth).
Mix well, cover with a lid and cook for 10 minutes (remember to keep on the low flame).
Remove the lid and add garam masala and freshly ground black pepper powder.
Cook until the desired consistency is achieved and serve hot with brown rice.

d23af349-20d5-49c0-9872-e75f1cb07792.name: Broccoli Chickpea Cur
d23af349-20d5-49c0-9872-e75f1cb07792.ingredients:
1 medium-sized head of broccoli, cut into florets
1 cup cooked chickpeas (soaked and cooked)
1 green bell pepper, sliced
1 zucchini, sliced
1 medium-sized carrot, sliced
1 tablespoon garlic-infused olive oil
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional for heat)
1 cup homemade coconut milk
1 tablespoon low-sodium tamari or soy sauce
Juice of 1 lime
Salt and pepper to taste
Fresh cilantro, for garnish
d23af349-20d5-49c0-9872-e75f1cb07792.steps:
In a large non-stick pan, heat the garlic-infused olive oil over medium heat.
Add the sliced bell pepper, zucchini, and carrot to the pan. Sauté for a few minutes until slightly tender.
Add the ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, and cayenne pepper (if using). Stir well to coat the vegetables with the spices.
Add the broccoli florets and cooked chickpeas to the pan. Stir to combine.
Pour in the coconut milk and low-sodium tamari or soy sauce. Stir gently to mix all the ingredients together.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let the curry simmer for about 15-20 minutes or until the broccoli is cooked to your desired tenderness.
Squeeze the lime juice over the curry and season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir well.
Remove from heat and garnish with fresh cilantro.
Serve the Broccoli Chickpea Curry with steamed brown rice or quinoa for a complete and satisfying meal.

83de3fd4-d50d-4657-9721-01d527be5103.name: Jowar Roti Wraps
83de3fd4-d50d-4657-9721-01d527be5103.ingredients:
1 cup jowar (sorghum) flour
1/2 cup firm tofu, drained and crumbled
1 cup shredded cruciferous vegetable (such as cabbage, kale, or broccoli)
1/2 cup chopped bell peppers
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro
1 teaspoon cumin powder
1 teaspoon coriander powder
1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
1/2 teaspoon red chili powder (adjust according to taste)
Salt to taste
Water (as needed)
83de3fd4-d50d-4657-9721-01d527be5103.steps:
In a non-stick pan over medium heat, add the crumbled tofu and cook until it starts to turn golden brown. Add the cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Mix well and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
In the same pan, add the shredded cruciferous vegetable and bell peppers. Sauté for a few minutes until they are slightly tender but still retain their crunch. Add the cooked tofu mixture to the pan, mix well, and cook for another 2 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the fresh cilantro.
Divide the jowar dough into 2 equal portions. Take one portion and roll it out into a thin circle on a clean surface using a rolling pin. Use some jowar flour to dust if necessary.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Place the rolled jowar roti on the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes on each side, until small brown spots appear. Repeat the process with the remaining dough.
Place a jowar roti on a clean surface and spoon half of the tofu and cruciferous vegetable filling onto one side of the roti. Fold the other half over the filling, pressing gently to seal the edges.
Repeat step 6 for the second roti. Cut the wraps in half and serve warm.

d391f2f0-f51b-47c0-b481-6f23dbac2dc8.name: Red lentil curry
d391f2f0-f51b-47c0-b481-6f23dbac2dc8.ingredients:
1 cup red lentils
2 cups water
1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon ground coriander
1 teaspoon ground turmeric
1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (adjust according to spice preference)
1 cup diced firm tofu
1 cup diced cruciferous vegetable (e.g., broccoli, cauliflower, or cabbage)
1 cup diced tomatoes
1 cup low-sodium vegetable broth
1 tablespoon tamari (gluten-free soy sauce)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro
Salt to taste
d391f2f0-f51b-47c0-b481-6f23dbac2dc8.steps:
Rinse the red lentils under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain and set aside.
In a large pot, combine the water, grated ginger, minced garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, and cayenne pepper. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
Add the red lentils to the pot, reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 15 minutes or until the lentils are tender and cooked through.
In the meantime, heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the diced tofu and cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Once the lentils are cooked, add the diced cruciferous vegetable, diced tomatoes, low-sodium vegetable broth, and tamari to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Cover the pot again and simmer for another 10-15 minutes or until the cruciferous vegetable is tender.
Add the cooked tofu to the pot and gently stir to incorporate.
Season with salt to taste and simmer for an additional 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and garnish with chopped fresh cilantro.
Serve the red lentil curry hot over steamed brown rice or quinoa.

aeb05c81-6b35-4947-9a05-7739397cc73c.name: Roasted pumpkin Sou
aeb05c81-6b35-4947-9a05-7739397cc73c.ingredients:
50 grams chunks of pumpkin
1 cup firm tofu, cubed
2 cups low FODMAP vegetable broth (check for suitable ingredients on the Monash University Low FODMAP Diet app)
1 cup cauliflower florets
1/2 teaspoon cumin
1/2 teaspoon paprika
1/2 teaspoon turmeric
1/4 teaspoon black pepper
Salt to taste
aeb05c81-6b35-4947-9a05-7739397cc73c.steps:
Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
Cut the pumpkin in half and remove the seeds and fibrous pulp. Place the pumpkin halves on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Roast the pumpkin in the preheated oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until the flesh is soft and easily scoopable with a spoon. Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly.
While the pumpkin is roasting, steam the cauliflower florets until tender. Set aside.
In a large pot, combine the roasted pumpkin flesh, tofu cubes, vegetable broth, cumin, paprika, turmeric, black pepper, and salt. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Using an immersion blender or a regular blender, puree the soup until smooth and creamy. If using a regular blender, allow the soup to cool slightly before blending in batches.
Return the pureed soup to the pot and add the steamed cauliflower florets. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.
Adjust the seasoning to taste and serve the roasted pumpkin soup hot.

8a69c69b-c074-430c-9896-94e7694d9eef.name: Tofu Stir fry
8a69c69b-c074-430c-9896-94e7694d9eef.ingredients:
1 cup firm tofu, drained and cubed
2 cups broccoli florets (75g per person)
1 cup sliced mushrooms
1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce
1 tablespoon rice vinegar
1 teaspoon grated ginger
2 green onions, sliced (green parts only, for low FODMAP)
1 tablespoon sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)
1 cup quinoa
2 cups water
8a69c69b-c074-430c-9896-94e7694d9eef.steps:
Rinse the quinoa under cold water to remove any bitter taste. In a saucepan, combine the rinsed quinoa and water. Bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 15-20 minutes. Once done, leave it covered for 5 min and fluff the quinoa and set aside.
In a non-stick skillet or wok, add the tofu cubes and cook over medium heat until lightly browned on all sides. Remove the tofu from the skillet and set aside.
Add the broccoli florets and mushrooms. Cook for about 5 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the chopped cruciferous vegetable to the skillet and cook for an additional 3 minutes until slightly tender.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce (or tamari), rice vinegar, and grated ginger. Pour the sauce over the vegetables in the skillet.
Return the tofu cubes to the skillet and stir-fry for another 2 minutes, allowing the flavors to blend. Remove the stir-fry from heat and sprinkle with green onions. Mix well.
Divide the quinoa into two plates, and spoon the tofu stir-fry over the quinoa. Garnish with sesame seeds, if desired. Serve the tofu stir-fry with quinoa immediately.

8fedd9f4-a327-4a9c-b0af-7468d95b7e83.name: Sweet Potato Hash
8fedd9f4-a327-4a9c-b0af-7468d95b7e83.ingredients:
1 medium sweet potato (50 grams)
5-6 raw walnuts coarsely chopped
1 tsp cumin seeds
1 tsp finely chopped green chili, without seeds
1 tsp salt
1 tbsp freshly squeezed lemon juice
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro for garnish
8fedd9f4-a327-4a9c-b0af-7468d95b7e83.steps:
Wash, dry, and peel the sweet potato. Grate them, place in a bowl and set aside. Alternatively you can bake the sweet potato for 15 minutes at 180 degrees
Using a food processor or dry spice grinder, grind the walnuts until they are coarsely ground. Be careful to not over-process; you don't want them to blend to a nut butter consistency. You may also coarsely chop them.
Dry roast cumin seeds for 15 seconds. Add the chilies and roast until slightly browned.
Add the grated sweet potatoes to the pan and sauté for 5 minutes, until softened. Season with the salt and mix until well combined.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 5 minutes, until almost cooked through.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and stir in the walnuts and lemon juice. Using a spatula, press down on the mixture, flattening it against the bottom of the pan. Continue to cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until a slight crust forms. Remove from the heat.
Garnish with the cilantro and serve immediately.

6fac1ae3-8c93-41c6-8b38-fa75f721b81e.name: KALE CRISPS
6fac1ae3-8c93-41c6-8b38-fa75f721b81e.ingredients:
1 bunch kale, thick stems removed (Limit to 50 grams)
10 cashews, soaked & drained.
1 fully roasted capsicum
1 tsp apple cider vinegar
1/4 tsp ground turmeric powder
1 tsp paprika
6fac1ae3-8c93-41c6-8b38-fa75f721b81e.steps:
Wash the kale leaves well and tear or cut large leaves into 2 inch pieces. Once dry, transfer to a large bowl and set aside.
Preheat oven to 180 degree celsius.
In a blender, combine 2 tbsp of water and rest of the ingredients mentioned until smooth. Sauce should be thick enough to coat the kale.
Pour the sauce on to the kale and toss to coat. Massage the sauce into the leaves.
Arrange the kales on to a baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes at 180 degree c.
Remove any pieces that are crisp and turn over any that are not yet crisp before the baking trays to the oven for longer or until the remaining kale pieces are crisp.
Be sure to watch so that they don't burn. Once done, set the hot kale crisps aside completely before eating.

eb8b4a49-c282-4f34-9cc4-d3a959247a0e.name: HUMMUS DIP
eb8b4a49-c282-4f34-9cc4-d3a959247a0e.ingredients:
2 large carrots, peeled and cut into sticks
1/2 cup cooked chickpeas
1 tablespoons tahini
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
1 teaspoon ground cumin
Salt to taste
Fresh parsley or paprika (optional, for garnish)
eb8b4a49-c282-4f34-9cc4-d3a959247a0e.steps:
Prepare the carrot sticks by peeling them and cutting them into sticks. Set aside
In a food processor, combine the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, ground cumin, of salt.
Process the mixture until smooth and creamy. If the mixture is too thick, add tablespoon at a time, and continue blending until you reach the desired consistency
Taste the hummus and adjust the seasoning if needed, adding more salt or lemon according to your preference.
Transfer the hummus to a serving bowl and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld together.
Serve the carrot sticks alongside the hummus. Enjoy!

a8f0e70b-77aa-4df8-afc7-b27b8d39d36f.name: MINT GAZPACHO
a8f0e70b-77aa-4df8-afc7-b27b8d39d36f.ingredients:
2 medium-sized cucumbers, peeled and seeds removed
1 cup fresh spinach leaves
1/2 cup fresh mint leaves
1 small green bell pepper, seeds removed
2 diced tomatoes (ensure portion)
1 tbsp fresh lime juice
1/4 teaspoon cumin
1/4 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup water
a8f0e70b-77aa-4df8-afc7-b27b8d39d36f.steps:
In a blender or food processor, add the cucumbers, spinach, mint leaves, green bell pepper, tomatoes, lime juice, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Blend the ingredients until smooth, gradually adding water as needed to achieve your desired consistency. If necessary, blend in batches.
Once the gazpacho is smooth and well combined, taste and adjust the seasonings if needed: salt, pepper, or lime juice according to your preference.
Transfer the gazpacho to a covered container and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to meld together.
Before serving, give the gazpacho a good stir. Pour into bowls or glasses and garnish with mint leaves if desired.
Enjoy the refreshing cucumber and mint gazpacho with your favorite side or serve as is.

4cb58c0a-717c-4ca2-97cc-f0d97110b982.name: BARNYARD RASAM RICE
4cb58c0a-717c-4ca2-97cc-f0d97110b982.ingredients:
40 grams barnyard millet
1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder
1 small tomato, chopped
1 small onion, chopped
1 small green chili, chopped
Salt to taste
2 cups water
Few curry leaves
Fresh coriander leaves for garnish
millets
water
onions
green chilies
tomatoes
turmeric powder
rasam powder
salt
fresh coriander leaves
4cb58c0a-717c-4ca2-97cc-f0d97110b982.steps:
Wash the millets thoroughly and soak in water overnight. Rinse and discard the water the next day.
Pour 2 cups of water into the pressure cooker and mix everything thoroughly.
Close the pressure cooker lid and cook on high heat until you get the first whistle.
Heat the pressure cooker over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and green chilies. Sauté until onions turn translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft and mushy.
Add washed millets to the pressure cooker. Stir well to combine with the onion-tomato mixture.
Now add turmeric powder, rasam powder, and salt to taste. Mix everything well.
Once you get the first whistle, reduce the heat to low and let it cook for about 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, turn off the heat and let the pressure release naturally.
Once the pressure is released, open the lid carefully. If the mixture is too thick, you can add a little hot water to adjust the consistency.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

b77d31db-ccbc-48ba-9033-a9be1beecf09.name: Chayote Chutney
b77d31db-ccbc-48ba-9033-a9be1beecf09.ingredients:
Chow chow (chayote) – 1 medium, peeled & cubed
G rated coconut – 1 tbsp
Green chilies – 2 (adjust spice)
Curry leaves – 6–8
Coriander leaves – 2 tbsp (fresh, chopped)
Mint leaves – 1 tbsp (optional, for freshness)
Dry roasted urad dal – 1 tbsp
(fo r thickness; can skip if avoiding dal)
Ginger – ½ inch piece
Salt – to taste
L emon juice – 1–2 tsp (for tang, since no tamarind)
b77d31db-ccbc-48ba-9033-a9be1beecf09.steps:
Steam or boil chow chow cubes until soft, cool slightly.
In a blender, grind: steamed chow chow, coconut, green chilies, ginger, cur ry leaves, coriander leaves, and mint leaves (if using).
Add salt and lemon juice. Blend smooth with little water.
D o a quick tempering with oil, mustard, curry leaves, and dry red chili; pour over chutney.

f0c3be90-187a-4a02-95bf-54b2f7b28e3a.name: ONE POT SESAME CARROT SOUP
f0c3be90-187a-4a02-95bf-54b2f7b28e3a.ingredients:
2 carrots, chopped
1/2 cup pumpkin, diced
1/2 cup cooked red lentils (masoor)
1/4 tsp turmeric powder
1/4 tsp cumin powder
2 tbsp tahini
Juice from 1 lemon
Salt to taste
Handful of mint leaves
f0c3be90-187a-4a02-95bf-54b2f7b28e3a.steps:
In a pan, saute all part 1 ingredients till fragrant (3-4 mins), sprinkle water if required.
Once fragrant, add 2.5 cups water and cook till the vegetables are tender. Turn off the heat and let the vegetables cool down.
Add this boiled mixture and part 2 ingredients, except mint leaves to a blender & blend to a smooth paste.
Transfer the soup back to the pan to warm the soup. Once warm, add in chopped mint leaves. Let it cook for 1-2 mins.
Turn off the heat & serve the soup immediately.
